title: Reimagining Forvo
coverAlt: A hand holding a smartphone, showing the proposed redesign of the Forvo mobile app.
excerpt: Forvo is a pronunciation app that offers "all the words in the world, pronounced". With this project, part of my extended education towards UX research, I focused on redesigning its mobile app through a new lens.

value.alt: A laptop showing the homepage of Forvo's website.
value.caption: Forvo's current website.

value.alt: Hands holding a smartphone, showing Forvo's mobile app homepage.
value.caption: The homepage of Forvo's mobile app.
Step 1: I searched the word کتاب;
Step 2: I listened to the pronunciation by tapping the "play" icon. After that, I decided to save it: I tapped the word کتاب, which led me to its page;
Step 3: I noticed different Persian pronunciations were available for this word;
Step 4: I tapped on the "more" icon beside one of them, scrolled down – and then tapped "Mark as favourite";
Step 5: A confirmation message told me the word got successfully saved. No other visual cues were left visible from this view, after it went away;

Step 6: I opened the "Favorites" tab, where one of the pronunciations of the word کتاب got saved, along many others of various meanings (in the list, there are words such as "mountain", "to draw", "turtle", the adverbial phrase "at least", and others).

sections.description: Adding a word to a collection: steps
Adding a word to a collection: description
Adding a word to a collection: suggestions

value.caption: First, language selection. Maya already has a target language — returning results across all languages adds noise. If her target isn't available, the system could offer to request a pronunciation, which Forvo already does.

Second, translation. Forvo offers translations, but only through a separate search. Displaying them directly alongside the word would help Maya connect pronunciation with meaning immediately — reducing cognitive load and strengthening retention.

Third, saving. A single "Favourites" folder loses usefulness as the collection grows — context disappears, and finding a specific word becomes its own obstacle. User-defined folders or collections would solve this simply.

sections.description: Adding a word, without losing the thread

value.caption: This opens a search page, already filtered to Japanese, clearly indicating she's adding words to this specific collection — inspired by Spotify's "Add to Playlist" workflow:

Maya can search for a word, view results, and either add the pronunciation to her collection right away or visit the word page for more context. If a result doesn't exist, she can request a pronunciation with a single tap.

User flow for adding a word to a collection, accounting for cases where a pronunciation isn’t in the database or an error occurs during saving.  Parkinson's Law informed this process: it revealed that the user doesn’t need to visit the word page to save it—a single tap from the search results can suffice if the pronunciation meets their needs.
